children.title: Education Department Workforce Falls Roughly 45% Between 2024 and 2026
children.description_short: An NPR report citing OPM data said the Education Department's headcount fell from about 4,200 in 2024 to 2,300 in 2026.
children.description_medium: An NPR story carried by KPBS reported that the U.S. Department of Education had roughly 4,200 employees in 2024 and 2,300 in 2026, a decline of about 45%, citing Office of Personnel Management data. The figures were reported during a May 2026 congressional hearing. The source does not give exact dates for either headcount or measure service effects.
children.description_long: An NPR story republished by KPBS on May 14, 2026 reported that the U.S. Department of Education's workforce had fallen from roughly 4,200 employees in 2024 to 2,300 in 2026, citing Office of Personnel Management data. The story described the difference as a roughly 45% reduction. It placed the figures in a House education committee hearing where Education Secretary Linda McMahon defended the administration's approach to shrinking the department and shifting some work. This card separates the staff comparison from distinct interagency agreements and budget proposals that had been bundled in the original record. The article does not give exact dates for the two OPM counts, identify which reductions came through layoffs rather than attrition, or quantify resulting service delays or student outcomes. It supports the approximate headcount comparison and the report date; it does not establish why each position ended or measure the effect on students. May 14 is the article's publication date, not a claim that all reductions happened that day.

children.title: Education Department Announces Six Interagency Agreements on November 18, 2025
children.description_short: Education announced six interagency agreements with Labor, Interior, HHS, and State to change administration of selected federal education programs.
children.description_medium: On November 18, 2025, the Education Department announced six interagency agreements with Labor, Interior, HHS, and State. The release described partner-agency roles in selected programs. For the K-12 agreement, it said Labor would manage competitions and provide technical assistance under Education Department oversight. It did not establish a transfer of statutory authority.
children.description_long: On November 18, 2025, the U.S. Department of Education announced six interagency agreements with the Departments of Labor, Interior, Health and Human Services, and State. The announcement described the agreements as changing administration of selected federal education programs and assigned partner agencies greater management roles. For the K-12 partnership, it said Labor would manage competitions and provide technical assistance with Education Department oversight. This card isolates that dated announcement from the June 2026 agreements and the separate staffing decline. The release does not substantiate the original record's claim that more than 100 programs were transferred without authorization. It describes interagency program management, and its K-12 section expressly says the arrangement remains under Education Department oversight. The release does not establish repeal of the department, transfer of its statutory policymaking authority, or the proposed FY2027 budget figure. The date is the official announcement date; this record concerns the agreements, not a later outcome measure.

children.title: Education Announces Four New Agreements on Disability Programs and Civil Rights
children.description_short: On June 16, 2026, Education announced four agreements with HHS and DOJ covering disability programs, civil-rights enforcement, and related services.
children.description_medium: On June 16, 2026, the Education Department announced four interagency agreements with HHS and DOJ. The release says HHS will partner on special education and rehabilitative services and DOJ on civil-rights enforcement, student privacy, and training. It says federal civil-rights enforcement will continue without interruption and ED will retain its statutory authority.
children.description_long: On June 16, 2026, the U.S. Department of Education announced four new interagency agreements with the Departments of Health and Human Services and Justice. The release says HHS will partner with Education on special education and rehabilitative services, while DOJ will partner on civil-rights enforcement, student privacy protection, and training and advisory services. The announcement states that federal civil-rights enforcement will continue without interruption and that the Education Department will retain all statutory authorities and functions. This card records the agreement announcement and its stated scope. It does not describe a completed transfer of statutory authority, a loss of all federal business or education support, or measurable effects on students and families. The source says these agreements followed 10 partnerships signed over the prior year; that broader history is not counted here. This entry focuses on the June 16 action rather than combining it with the November 2025 agreements, the staffing comparison, or a proposed FY2027 budget reduction. Later implementation evidence would be needed to quantify operational changes or outcomes.
